title: 320. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the defining property of parallel lines in a plane.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes parallel lines in the same plane?

options.label: A
options.text: They never intersect and are always the same distance apart.

options.label: B
options.text: They always intersect at exactly one point.

questions.explanation: Parallel lines in the same plane are lines that do not intersect, no matter how far they are extended. They also remain the same perpendicular distance apart. Therefore, the correct description is that they never intersect and are always the same distance apart.
questions.hint: Recall the definition of parallel lines in a plane and what happens when they are extended.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the defining property of perpendicular lines.
questions.question: Which statement correctly defines perpendicular lines?

options.label: A
options.text: They intersect to form four right angles.

options.label: B
options.text: They never meet and stay the same distance apart.

questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines are two lines that intersect at a right angle. When two lines are perpendicular, the intersection forms four right angles, each measuring \(90^\circ\). Therefore, the correct definition is that they intersect to form four right angles.
questions.hint: Think about the angle formed when two lines are perpendicular.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the slope of a line perpendicular to a given line.
questions.question: Line \(l_1\) has slope \( \frac{2}{3} \). What is the slope of a line \(l_2\) that is perpendicular to \(l_1\)?
questions.explanation: For two nonvertical perpendicular lines, the product of their slopes is \(-1\). Thus, the slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal of the given slope. The negative reciprocal of \( \frac{2}{3} \) is \( -\frac{3}{2} \). Therefore, the slope of \(l_2\) is \( -\frac{3}{2} \).
questions.hint: Use the rule that perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals of each other.

questions.concept: Slope of a Line Parallel to a Given Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the slope of a line parallel to a given line from its equation.
questions.question: What is the slope of a line parallel to the line \(3x - 4y = 8\)?
questions.explanation: Rewrite the given equation in slope-intercept form. Starting with \(3x - 4y = 8\), subtract \(3x\) from both sides: \(-4y = -3x + 8\). Dividing by \(-4\) gives \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 2\). The slope of the given line is \( \frac{3}{4} \). Parallel lines have equal slopes, so a parallel line also has slope \( \frac{3}{4} \).
questions.hint: First rewrite the equation in the form \(y = mx + b\), then identify the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.concept: Alternate Interior Angles with Parallel Lines
questions.learningObjective: Apply the alternate interior angles property to find an unknown angle measure.
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle measures \(65^\circ\). What is the measure of its alternate interior angle?
questions.explanation: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are equal. Since the given interior angle measures \(65^\circ\), its alternate interior angle also measures \(65^\circ\). Therefore, the correct measure is \(65^\circ\).
questions.hint: Recall the relationship between alternate interior angles when the two lines are parallel.

questions.concept: Consecutive Interior Angles with Parallel Lines
questions.learningObjective: Apply the consecutive interior angles property to calculate an angle measure.
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of consecutive interior angles are supplementary. If one angle measures \(110^\circ\), what is the measure of the other angle?
questions.explanation: Consecutive interior angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines are supplementary, meaning their measures add to \(180^\circ\). Therefore, the other angle is \(180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ\). The correct measure is \(70^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation of the perpendicular bisector of a segment.
questions.question: Segment \(AB\) has endpoints \(A(2,1)\) and \(B(6,5)\). Which equation represents the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\)?
questions.explanation: The midpoint of \(AB\) is \(\left(\frac{2+6}{2}, \frac{1+5}{2}\right) = (4,3)\). The slope of \(AB\) is \(\frac{5-1}{6-2} = \frac{4}{4} = 1\). A perpendicular bisector must have slope \(-1\), the negative reciprocal of \(1\). Using point-slope form with midpoint \((4,3)\): \(y - 3 = -1(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(y = -x + 7\). Therefore, the perpendicular bisector is \(y = -x + 7\).
questions.hint: Find the midpoint and the slope of \(AB\), then use the negative reciprocal slope for the perpendicular bisector.

questions.learningObjective: Analyze equations to determine whether two lines are parallel or perpendicular.
questions.question: What is the relationship between the lines \(y = 3x + 2\) and \(6x - 2y = 4\)?
questions.explanation: Rewrite \(6x - 2y = 4\) in slope-intercept form. Subtract \(6x\) from both sides: \(-2y = -6x + 4\). Dividing by \(-2\) gives \(y = 3x - 2\). Both lines have slope \(3\), and parallel lines have equal slopes. Therefore, the two lines are parallel.
questions.hint: Rewrite the second equation in slope-intercept form and compare the slopes.

questions.concept: Lines Perpendicular to the Same Line
questions.learningObjective: Reason about the relationship between two lines perpendicular to the same line in a plane.
questions.question: In a plane, two distinct lines are both perpendicular to the same line. What is the relationship between the two lines?

options.label: A
options.text: They are perpendicular to each other.

options.label: B
options.text: They are parallel to each other.

questions.explanation: In a plane, if two distinct lines are perpendicular to the same line, then both lines make a \(90^\circ\) angle with that line. This means they have the same direction and do not intersect. Therefore, the two lines are parallel to each other.
questions.hint: Consider what happens to the direction of two lines that are both at \(90^\circ\) to the same line.

questions.learningObjective: Infer a perpendicular relationship using parallel line properties.
questions.question: In a plane, line \(m\) is parallel to line \(n\). Line \(p\) is perpendicular to line \(m\). What is the relationship between line \(p\) and line \(n\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(m \parallel n\), lines \(m\) and \(n\) have the same direction. If line \(p\) is perpendicular to line \(m\), it forms a \(90^\circ\) angle with \(m\). Because \(n\) is parallel to \(m\), line \(p\) must also form a \(90^\circ\) angle with \(n\). Therefore, line \(p\) is perpendicular to line \(n\).
questions.hint: Use the fact that a line perpendicular to one of two parallel lines is also perpendicular to the other.
